title: Count Distinct Subsequences Matching a Target
statement: Given two strings s and t, count how many distinct ways t appears as a subsequence of s. A single occurrence is a set of indices in s, strictly increasing, whose characters read in that order spell t exactly; two occurrences are considered distinct if and only if their index sets differ (not the letters they land on). Return that count as an integer. If t is longer than s, or t cannot be formed from s at all, return 0. The empty string t can always be formed exactly one way (by choosing no indices), so when t is empty return 1. Example: for s = 'rabbbit' and t = 'rabbit' there are 3 distinct index sets, so the answer is 3.
hints: Think about scanning s one character at a time while asking how many characters of t you have matched so far. What two independent positions describe your state?

Let dp[i][j] be the number of distinct ways to spell the first j characters of t using the first i characters of s, with dp[i][0] = 1 for every i since the empty target is always formed by choosing nothing.

For each s[i-1] you always inherit dp[i-1][j] (the ways that decline to use s[i-1]); additionally, when s[i-1] == t[j-1] you add dp[i-1][j-1] (the ways that use s[i-1] to match t[j-1]). The match branch alone is not enough because a repeated matching letter can be used or skipped.
